funFacts.text: The first video game, "Tennis for Two" (1958), ran on an analog oscilloscope at a science fair. The creator made it because the open house was boring.
Floppy disks were called "floppy" because the original 8-inch disks bent in your hand. The 3.5" disks we remember were technically rigid.
Python is named after Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake. Guido van Rossum was reading the scripts when he picked the name in 1991.
The QWERTY layout was designed in 1873 to slow typists down — keys jammed on mechanical typewriters. We've kept it ever since.
Java was almost called "Oak" — until lawyers found another product with that name. The team picked Java over coffee. Literally.
The first computer virus, "Creeper" (1971), just displayed: "I'm the creeper, catch me if you can!" The first antivirus, "Reaper", was made to hunt it.
The first computer mouse was made of wood (1964). Doug Engelbart's prototype had two perpendicular wheels — and one button.
The save icon (a floppy disk) is now older than most of the people who use it. Kids today have never touched one.
The password 'password' is still used by millions of people every year. It takes less than 1 second to crack.
Over 5.5 billion people use the internet today — more than have access to clean toilets.
The average office worker receives 121 emails per day. About 49% of all email traffic is spam.
The word 'computer' originally meant a person who does calculations. It was a job title until the 1950s.
A modern car has more lines of code (~100 million) than a Boeing 787 Dreamliner, Facebook, and the Large Hadron Collider combined.
The average software has 15-50 bugs per 1,000 lines of code. NASA's Space Shuttle had just 0.1 bugs per 1,000 lines.
The entire data of Wikipedia (text only) is about 22 GB — it fits on a cheap USB stick.
The first MP3 ever encoded was 'Tom's Diner' by Suzanne Vega (1993). Engineers chose it because of her clear, unaccompanied voice.
Bitcoin mining uses more electricity annually than the entire country of Argentina.
The Apollo 11 guidance computer had 74 KB of memory. Your phone has about 80 million times more.
The first YouTube video ever uploaded was 'Me at the zoo' (2005). It's 18 seconds long and features elephants.
The average person touches their phone 2,617 times a day. Heavy users exceed 5,400 touches.
Google processes over 8.5 billion searches per day — that's about 99,000 per second.
GitHub's Arctic Code Vault stores open-source code on film reels in a decommissioned coal mine in Svalbard, Norway. It's designed to last 1,000 years.
Minecraft's world is 8x the surface area of Earth. The procedural generation uses a single seed number to create it all.
The first 1 GB hard drive (1980) weighed 550 pounds, was the size of a refrigerator, and cost $40,000.
It takes more computing power to run a modern AI model once than it took to send humans to the Moon.
npm (Node Package Manager) has over 2 million packages. The average JavaScript project installs over 1,000 dependencies.
The most expensive cybersecurity breach in history was Yahoo (2013) — 3 billion accounts compromised. It reduced their sale price by $350 million.
Linux runs on 100% of the world's top 500 supercomputers. Not 99%. All of them.
Amazon calculated that every 100ms of latency costs them 1% in sales. Google found that an extra 0.5s in search page load drops traffic by 20%.
The entire Lord of the Rings trilogy took 12 TB of storage for rendering. A single frame took up to 48 hours to render.
There are over 700 programming languages in active use. Most programmers only ever learn 3-5 in their career.
The first website (info.cern.ch) is still online. It explains what the World Wide Web is.
1 gram of DNA can theoretically store 215 petabytes (215 million gigabytes) of data.
SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket runs Linux. The flight software is written in C++.
Stack Overflow has over 24 million answered questions. The most viewed question is about reverting a Git commit.
Siri was originally developed as a DARPA-funded AI project. Apple acquired it for $200 million in 2010.
90% of the world's data was created in the last two years. We generate 2.5 quintillion bytes daily.
The first webcam was pointed at a coffee pot at Cambridge University (1991). Researchers used it to check if the pot was empty before walking downstairs.
The Game Boy (1989) had less computing power than a modern smart doorbell. It sold 118 million units.
The internet's undersea cables total over 1.3 million km — enough to wrap around Earth 33 times. 97% of intercontinental data travels through them.
Thomas Edison's lab made the first audio recording (1877) and also the first motion picture (1891). Both technologies were side projects.
The word 'robot' comes from the Czech word 'robota' meaning forced labor. It was coined in a 1920 play by Karel Čapek.
The hex color code for Facebook blue (#4267B2) was chosen because Mark Zuckerberg is red-green colorblind. Blue is the color he sees best.
The original source code for the World Wide Web was written on a NeXT computer. Steve Jobs founded NeXT after being fired from Apple.
The entire internet weighs about 50 grams — the combined weight of all the electrons in motion carrying data at any given moment.
A single Google search uses about 0.3 Wh of energy — enough to light a 60W bulb for 18 seconds.
The Easter egg tradition started in 1980 when an Atari developer hid his name in Adventure because the company refused to credit programmers.
PHP originally stood for 'Personal Home Page'. Its creator, Rasmus Lerdorf, said he never intended it to become a real programming language.
The first domain name ever registered was symbolics.com on March 15, 1985. It's still active as a historical museum.
Netflix's recommendation engine saves the company $1 billion per year by reducing customer churn.

On September 9, 1947, the Harvard Mark II malfunctioned — engineers found a moth stuck in relay #70 and taped it into the logbook: "First actual case of bug being found." The moth is still in the Smithsonian.
Ray Tomlinson picked the @ symbol for email in 1971 simply because it was already on the keyboard and almost nobody used it. One arbitrary choice — now it's in every email address on Earth.

Arrays start at index 0 because of memory math: address = start + index × element_size. With 0-based indexing the first element needs no offset — in the 1950s that saved a subtraction on every single array access.

In 2002 a sysadmin got a bug report: "we can't send email farther than 500 miles." It was real — a misconfigured ~3 ms mail timeout only let messages reach servers within the distance light travels in that time.

quotes.text: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.
quotes.author: Linus Torvalds

quotes.text: First, solve the problem. Then, write the code.
quotes.author: John Johnson

quotes.text: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.
quotes.author: Alan Kay

quotes.text: Simplicity is the soul of efficiency.
quotes.author: Austin Freeman

quotes.text: It's not a bug — it's an undocumented feature.

quotes.text: It works on my machine.

quotes.text: The best error message is the one that never shows up.
quotes.author: Thomas Fuchs

quotes.text: Walking on water and developing software from a specification are easy if both are frozen.
quotes.author: Edward V. Berard

quotes.text: Programming today is a race between software engineers trying to build bigger and better idiot-proof programs, and the Universe trying to produce bigger and better idiots.
quotes.author: Rick Cook

quotes.text: Always code as if the guy who ends up maintaining your code will be a violent psychopath who knows where you live.
quotes.author: John Woods

quotes.text: There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things.
quotes.author: Phil Karlton

quotes.text: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.
quotes.author: Arthur C. Clarke

quotes.text: The Internet is becoming the town square for the global village of tomorrow.
quotes.author: Bill Gates

quotes.text: Privacy is not something that I'm merely entitled to, it's an absolute prerequisite.
quotes.author: Marlon Brando

quotes.text: Information is power. But like all power, there are those who want to keep it for themselves.
quotes.author: Aaron Swartz

quotes.text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
quotes.author: Alan Turing

quotes.text: People think that computer science is the art of geniuses, but the actual reality is the opposite — just many people doing things that build on each other.

quotes.text: The best code is no code at all.
quotes.author: Jeff Atwood

quotes.text: Move fast and break things. Unless you are breaking stuff, you are not moving fast enough.
quotes.author: Mark Zuckerberg

quotes.text: The Web as I envisaged it, we have not seen it yet. The future is still so much bigger than the past.
quotes.author: Tim Berners-Lee

quotes.text: Real artists ship.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.text: Everybody should learn to program a computer, because it teaches you how to think.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.text: Most good programmers do programming not because they expect to get paid, but because it is fun to program.
quotes.author: Linus Torvalds

quotes.text: Unix is simple. It just takes a genius to understand its simplicity.
quotes.author: Dennis Ritchie

quotes.text: Controlling complexity is the essence of computer programming.
quotes.author: Brian Kernighan

quotes.text: Programming is the art of telling another human being what one wants the computer to do.
quotes.author: Donald Knuth

quotes.text: Java is to JavaScript what car is to carpet.
quotes.author: Chris Heilmann

quotes.text: In a room full of top software designers, if two agree on the same thing, that's a majority.
quotes.author: Bill Curtis

quotes.text: Programming isn't about what you know; it's about what you can figure out.
quotes.author: Chris Pine

quotes.text: The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge.
quotes.author: Daniel J. Boorstin

quotes.text: Weeks of coding can save you hours of planning.
quotes.author: Anonymous

quotes.text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.
quotes.author: Kent Beck

timeline.title: ARPANET sends its first message
timeline.text: UCLA → Stanford. They tried to send LOGIN, the system crashed after 'LO'. Humanity's first internet packet was a typo.

timeline.title: The internet is born on a Tuesday
timeline.text: January 1, 1983 — ARPANET switches from NCP to TCP/IP. Networks of networks become possible. Vint Cerf calls it "Flag Day".

timeline.title: Linus posts to comp.os.minix
timeline.text: "Hello everybody out there using minix — I'm doing a (free) operating system (just a hobby, won't be big and professional like gnu)." It would become the most successful OS in history.

timeline.title: Java is released — "Write Once, Run Anywhere"
timeline.text: Sun Microsystems ships Java 1.0. The JVM concept revolutionizes how we ship software. JavaScript is created the same year by Brendan Eich, in 10 days.

timeline.title: Linus writes Git in two weeks
timeline.text: After BitKeeper revoked the Linux kernel's free license, Linus built a distributed version control system from scratch. He named it after himself: "I'm an egotistical bastard."

timeline.title: The iPhone redefines a computer
timeline.text: A computer in your pocket, with no keyboard, running custom UNIX. Within a decade more code runs on phones than on every desktop ever made.
